creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The Codex adapter writes each delegate to `~/.codex/delegates/<name>.md` and warns `Codex does not natively consume delegate assets - installed as passive reference file`. Codex now loads custom agents: one TOML file per agent in `~/.codex/agents/` (or `.codex/agents/` per project), with required `name`, `description` and `developer_instructions`, and optional `model`, `model_reasoning_effort` and `sandbox_mode` ([docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents)). Until tai writes those, a Codex agent cannot spawn a delegate by name and a delegate's `model` never applies, so every skill that tells the agent to spawn a reviewer delegate needs a Codex-specific branch.

Probably: write each delegate as `agents/<name>.toml`, with the body as `developer_instructions`, `model` from the delegate's model field, and `tools` mapped to `sandbox_mode` or dropped with a warning. The code is `transformDelegate` and the `delegate: "delegates"` entry in the asset mapping in `internal/adapter/codex/codex.go`, with tests in `codex_test.go` (one asserts the passive-reference warning). These are new files rather than edits to `config.toml`, so the `ConfigWriteConsent` prompt does not apply.

Things to check:

- That the installed Codex reads `~/.codex/agents`. The docs say current releases do; the report was on 0.160.x and did not verify it.
- What a Codex install does with a delegate `model` written for Claude Code (`sonnet`, `opus`). Dropping it with a warning is likely right.
- That the next install removes the old `~/.codex/delegates/*.md` files once the mapping changes.

(Moved from GitHub issue #12, part 3.)
title: Install delegates as Codex custom agents
